_comment: COLLECTIVE EDGE COLOR TOKENS. Mirrors snippets/palette.css exactly, plus logo and type pointers. Read by generators that cannot parse CSS: python-pptx, python-docx, matplotlib, reportlab, and any script emitting PPTX, DOCX, XLSX or PDF. Type values are NOT duplicated here. If a value here disagrees with palette.css, palette.css wins and this file is stale.
_shape: One key structure in all three kits; scripts/check-sync.py fails when the keys drift. Values differ, keys do not. Top level: identity strings (brand, name, role, parent, prefix, hasColor, version, typeSystemVersion, cdnRoot, paletteCss, dataColorCss, typeTokensJson, colorNote). raw: LIST of the brand's own --<prefix>-* colors, each {key, var, hex, rgb, pantone, use}; the list length differs by brand. neutral: the shared neutral family, each {var, hex, rgb, use}. foreground, background, border: the semantic layer, keyed by the CSS name without its dashes prefix, each {var, value, hex, rgb, alpha, use}; hex and rgb are null where the value is not a solid color. tiers: the surface ladder from darkest to lightest, plus tableHeader and focusRing. alert: the canonical functional family, go warn stop info, each {var, base, text, tint, onTint, onDark, use}, with the measured worst ratios in contrast. status: the --status-* aliases of alert, each {var, aliasOf, hex, rgb, onDark, use}. diagramRoles: decision, warning, process, connector, shape, and brandRoles, a LIST that is empty unless the brand adds a role. data: series, sequential, diverging, direction, comparison, chrome; sequential is the one block whose values differ by brand. logos: every role name used in brands.json, null where the brand ships no such file, then minWidth, minWidthPrint, viewBox, aspect, fill, clearSpace, source, notes. cobrandMarks: LIST of {partner, on-light, on-dark}, empty outside the parent brand. type: pointers to the shared type layer, never type values. radius, shadow, motion: identical in every kit. A null means the brand has no such value. A LIST may be empty; an object never drops a key.
name: Collective Edge
colorNote: Collective Edge has no hue of its own. It reads as tiers: black is the hero and the accent, graphite #23232A is the band and the body ink, #4E4F58 is the mid tone, and two tints step the page. White is the document surface, and any color on a CE surface belongs to a partner or to the alert family.

raw.use: Hero, title slides, section dividers, accent
Header band. The shared neutral ink
Body text on light. The shared neutral ink
Dimmed non-text marks. 3.39:1 on white, so never text at any size
The Edge wedge when CE stands alone, and the band rule. Never text
Stronger surface tint, table header fill
The Edge wedge, CE standing alone
The Edge wedge on a Royal co-brand surface
The Edge wedge on an Apex co-brand surface

neutral._comment: The shared neutral family. Identical in every brand. OKLCH hue 280, chroma under 0.016, so it sits between the Apex and Royal hues and leans toward neither. Ratios are on #FFFFFF.

tertiary.use: Tertiary text, metadata. 5.12:1. The dimmest text

dimmed.use: Dimmed non-text marks. 3.39:1, so never text

mid.use: Mid tone fill. White on it measures 8.13:1

onDarkCaption.use: Captions and eyebrows on a band

foreground._comment: Semantic layer. Identical variable names in every brand, so a component written for one brand renders correctly in another with only palette.css swapped. Ratios are the worst of #FFFFFF and this brand's bg-surface.

fg-3.use: Tertiary text, metadata. 4.53:1. The dimmest text

fg-4.use: Dimmed non-text marks. 3.00:1, so never text

fg-accent.use: Brand-colored text. CE has no hue, so the accent is black over graphite ink. 18.59:1. It measures 1.35:1 against fg-1, so it separates from body text at display size only

fg-on-dark-1.use: Primary text on dark. 15.61:1 on bg-band

background._comment: bg-surface-2 and bg-mid complete the surface ladder; see tiers.

bg-surface-2.use: Stronger tint, table header fill. 1.25:1 against white. fg-3 measures 4.10:1 here, so set fg-2

bg-mid.use: Mid tone filled block. White on it measures 8.13:1

bg-band.use: Header band. Graphite, one step up from the black hero

border-band-rule.use: Accent rule under the band. The standalone wedge gray. 9.33:1 on the band

tiers._comment: Collective Edge runs on tiers, not on a hue. Darkest to lightest: black hero, graphite band, mid tone, two tints, white. A table header sits on surface2, with a 1.5pt (2px) #000000 rule under the header row.

focusRing.css: --ui-focus-ring in snippets/ui.css, which reads --focus-ring from palette.css, here --ce-black, and --fg-on-dark-1 under .ui-on-dark

alert._comment: The alert family. CANONICAL, and identical in every brand so an operational signal never changes meaning between documents. It is the one source for status, direction and diagram colors. Five steps each: base is a fill, rule or dot on a light ground; text is text on white and on every surface tint; tint is the pill and callout fill; onTint is text on that tint; onDark is text, dots and rules on a band. A brand accent is never an alert color. Always paired with an icon or a word.

go.use: Cleared, on time, in service, favorable. White on the base measures 5.32:1

warn.use: At risk, pending, watch, caution. The base measures 3.40:1 on white and is a fill, a rule or a dot, never text; ink on the base measures 4.59:1

stop.use: Failed, out of service, blocked, unfavorable. White on the base measures 6.29:1

info.use: Neutral notice. White on the base measures 7.14:1

contrast._comment: Worst measured ratio across white, the three brand surfaces and the three brand bands, in the order go, warn, stop, info.

status._comment: Aliases of the alert base, kept so everything already reading them resolves. In CSS they follow the ground: under .bk-on-dark they resolve to the onDark step. For warn as text read alert.warn.text.

warn.use: Attention amber. A fill, never text

diagramRoles._comment: Identical in every brand so a diagram reads the same regardless of whose document it sits in. Rectangles, 6px radius. Role is communicated by fill, never by shape. The fills are the alert and neutral families; never invent a hue for a role. Each role names the text color that clears contrast on its own fill; measured, do not substitute.

warning.textRule: ink, not white. White on this amber measures 3.40:1 and fails at body size

data._comment: HOUSE DATA COLOR. Mirrors snippets/data-color.css, which is identical in every kit. A brand accent is never a series color and no slot is remapped. Collective Edge is monochromatic and takes the house series unchanged. Verify any set with scripts/validate-palette.py. Reasoning and measured numbers in reference/data-color.md.

series._comment: Categorical identity. Assign IN ORDER, never cycle, never generate an eighth. The order is the color-blindness safety mechanism. Worst neighboring pair: dE 16.3 simulated red-green and 20.3 normal vision on light, 11.6 and 16.9 on a dark ground. All seven measure 3:1 or better on white and 3.55:1 or better on every band. Cap of 4 on scatter, bubble, map and small multiples on light, 3 on a dark ground.

sequential._comment: Magnitude. One hue, light to dark. The one data block whose values differ by brand: darker means more in any hue, so the ramp carries the brand. Collective Edge has no hue, so its ramp is the neutral and lands on fg-1 #23232A at step 700. Steps 100 and 200 are for continuous scales only. Discrete ordered marks start at step 300. On a dark ground the anchor flips: the lightest step means the largest value.

diverging._comment: Polarity, distance above or below a baseline. Poles are red and blue, NOT red and green: red against green measures dE 5.5 under simulated deuteranopia and collapses into one color. Red against blue measures dE 23.6 at the furthest step under the weaker red-green simulation, 24.5 on a dark ground. The blue is the hue of series 1, stepped to the lightness of the red at every step. The midpoint is gray on purpose, because a hue there reads as a value rather than as no difference.

direction._comment: Is this good news. Aliases of the alert family. Color follows favorable against unfavorable. It NEVER follows the arithmetic sign of the delta and never the direction of the arrow: a cost falling and transports rising are both favorable. Every value ships with an arrow or icon AND a word. hex is text on the page and a fill; ink is text on the matching tint. On a dark ground the tint is the dark step at 18 percent and the ink on it is white.

comparison._comment: The before-and-after chart. Two tints of the brand hue is the defect this layer exists to fix: they are too close to separate, so the reader has to read the labels. An inert gray baseline against series 1 reads instantly.

baseline.use: the prior period. Inert, and nothing to feel about it

comparison.variant: On a single-metric hero slide the result bar may take the direction color instead. One slide, not a deck: if every bar is green, green stops carrying information.

chrome._comment: Recessive by policy. The grid is a hint, never a feature. The shared neutrals.

logos._comment: Ask for a role, never for a filename. Partner kits map the same roles to different filenames. `-on-light` is the version to place ON a light background. Collective Edge ships no compact lockup, no stacked lockup and no app icon.
notes: The Edge wedge is the one part of the block mark that carries color, and that color is the PARTNER's. Every combination ships as a file; see cobrandMarks. Never hand-recolor a mark.

type._comment: Pointers only. Shared across the house and served from the Collective Edge kit, so there is one font file and one place to update it. Sizes, weights, leading, tracking and measure live in type-tokens.json and are never duplicated here.

shadow._comment: The house is flat. Shadow signals elevation, never decoration.
